title: "Quickstart: conditional GVAR on synthetic data"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Quickstart: conditional GVAR on synthetic data}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r}
library(preJCERBGVAR)
sim <- jcer_simulate_gvar(n_countries = 3, n_obs = 120, seed = 42, contemporaneous = FALSE)
fit <- jcer_bgvar(sim$data, sim$W, draws = 100, seed = 42, contemporaneous = FALSE)
summary(fit)
ir <- jcer_irf(fit, "US.r_short", c("JP.r_short", "JP.y"), horizon = 12,
               identification = "generalized", shock_bp = 25)
plot(ir)
```

All observations and figures are synthetic. Generalized innovations do not
identify a pure Fed policy causal effect. Rates default to percent points:
25 basis points equals 0.25, or 0.0025 with `rate_unit="decimal"`.
The rate unit is explicit metadata; the fitter never rescales observations.
Transform GDP/prices to a suitable stationary scale before fitting real data.
The default prior is not invariant to rescaling: use appropriately rescaled
`prior_control` when comparing percent and decimal parameterizations.

The fit contains country coefficient/covariance draws and posterior parameters,
prepared regressions and E/H maps, usable world draws, stage timings, posterior
target text, and counts/reasons for excluded draws. Input matrices must share
variable names and sample rows; unlabeled matrices assume aligned observations.

`cores=2` uses independent country RNG seeds and produces identical country
draws to `cores=1`. Small jobs may be slower because workers must start.
Seeded calls restore the caller's RNG state. Changing draw count preserves
the prefix within every country's draws.
